text: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
An experiment is completed to find the percentage by mass of copper in a sample of brass.
In the experiment, the sample of brass is reacted with an excess of concentrated nitric acid, HNO .
This forms a solution containing Cu (aq) ions. The amount of Cu (aq) ions formed is determined
by titration.
A student uses the following method.
step 1 Weigh a glass beaker and record the mass.
step 2 Add approximately 1.00 g of powdered brass to the beaker and record the mass of the
beaker and the brass.
step 3 Transfer the brass into conical flask A which contains excess concentrated HNO .
step 4 Reweigh the glass beaker and record the mass.
step 5 Add aqueous sodium carbonate, Na CO (aq), dropwise to flask A until a precipitate of
copper(II) carbonate, CuCO (s), appears. Then add dilute ethanoic acid dropwise until
the precipitate is fully dissolved.
step 6 Transfer all the contents of flask A to a 100.0 cm volumetric flask and make up to the
mark with distilled water. This is solution B.
step 7 Transfer 10.0 cm of solution B into conical flask C.
step 8 Add 10 cm , an excess, of aqueous potassium iodide, KI(aq), to flask C.
step 9 Titrate the contents of flask C against 0.0600 mol dm sodium thiosulfate, Na S O (aq),
using starch solution as an indicator.
step 10 Repeat steps 7 to 9 until concordant results are obtained.

text: Ester X has the formula CH COOR.
R is an alkyl group with the general formula C H .
n 2n+1
Ester X undergoes alkaline hydrolysis with aqueous potassium hydroxide, KOH(aq).
The resulting mixture is acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid, HCl (aq).
The organic products of the hydrolysis after acidification are ethanoic acid, CH COOH, and an
alcohol, ROH. Once the identity of ROH is found, the structure of ester X can then be determined.
A student uses the following steps.
step 1 Equal molar quantities of ester X and KOH(aq) are placed in a round‑bottomed flask.
step 2 A few drops of a suitable indicator are added to show whether a reaction has occurred.
step 3 A substance is added to promote smooth boiling.
step 4 The reaction mixture is set up for reflux and heated for 30 minutes.
step 5 After 30 minutes, the reaction mixture in the round‑bottomed flask is acidified by adding
HCl (aq) dropwise.
step 6 Thin‑layer chromatography is carried out on the reaction mixture.
